chosen.criterion_applied: Every unsafe operation is one enumerated call to `engine_table_cleanup(<module-static slot>)`; the caller set is a single internal cleanup-stack walk with no caller-supplied pointer; the nine are one mechanically identical class and the pattern is reusable for engine static-table cleanup.
chosen.why_not_count: The 9 are chosen for enumerability and caller-contract establishability, not because they are few. Their caller contract is the smallest in the closure that is still a real, reusable ABI edge.

rejected_alternatives.reason: 31 extension files with heterogeneous callback signatures and per-extension ownership; every unsafe op and caller contract cannot be enumerated in one auditable package with the available evidence. The p25-x509 receipt still records 64 BLOCKED boundaries.
Spans provider key management, legacy digest init, SLH-DSA (32 sites) and multiple distinct ownership interiors. Largest volume and not a single reusable caller contract.

Smallest by count but not one mechanism (namemap vs thread). Establishing it requires concurrency evidence (Miri/Loom/TSan) that is NOT_RUN for those units; count alone is explicitly not the criterion.
The mechanism is CONTRACTED with 73 unaudited SSL BIO call sites; the two closure sites cannot support a mechanism-scope discharge.
Heterogeneous sub-mechanisms (DRBG vs CMS vs store; session ciph/conf/rsa) that each need per-site ownership analysis. Deferred, not rejected on principle.

caller_contract_shared.invocation_path: ENGINE_register_* or ENGINE_set_default_* -> engine_table_register (src/engine/eng_table.rs:273-296) -> engine_cleanup_add_first(cleanup) only when the table slot was NULL -> CLEANUP_STACK -> [withheld engine_cleanup_int] -> engine_cleanup_cb_free(item) -> cb() (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:684-694).
caller_contract_shared.registration_cardinality: At most one cleanup item per table slot lifetime: `engine_cleanup_add_first` runs only when `table.load().is_null()` (the `added` arm), and the slot is only returned to NULL by the cleanup that is currently unreachable. A second register/set_default on the same slot does not enqueue again.
caller_preconditions: Zero arguments: no caller-supplied pointer, extent, alignment or initialisation state.
The cleanup item stores the module's own function item (`Some(engine_unregister_all_*)`); no other writer targets CLEANUP_STACK with these nine (CALLER_SET/STATIC_PAIRING controls PASS).
The engine lock is initialised and not held by this thread at invocation (authority eng_lib.c:169-184: callbacks run before CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_free; the callback takes the write lock itself).
No re-entrant engine API is active on this thread (B20 external contract: engine init/finish/destroy hooks must not re-enter; recursive write acquisition is refused).
implementation_may_assume: The slot is the module's own process-global `&'static EngineTableSlot`.
The lhash and EnginePile nodes are owned by the slot and released exactly once by `engine_table_cleanup` under the write lock.
A second invocation observes NULL and is a no-op.
caller_contract_shared.not_assumed: No caller-provided table, key, pointer or length. There is no wrong-arity, wrong-extent or uninitialised-argument obligation on this class.

caller_contract.who_may_call: Only `engine_cleanup_cb_free` (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:684-694), as the `sk_*_pop_free` callback of `engine_cleanup_int` (`engine_cleanup_cb_free(item)` -> `cb()`). `engine_cleanup_int` is withheld (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:696-700), so no invocation executes at this identity. `engine_cleanup_add_first` is the only writer that enqueues this pointer, and only `engine_table_register` reaches it (src/engine/eng_table.rs:294-296).
preconditions_the_caller_must_establish: The pointer stored in the cleanup item is exactly this module's function item (guaranteed by `Some(cb)` at the two registration sites and by no other writer; CALLER_SET/STATIC_PAIRING controls PASS).
Zero arguments: there is no pointer, extent, alignment or initialisation state supplied by the caller.

The engine read/write lock is initialised and is not held by this thread when `cb()` runs (authority crypto/engine/eng_lib.c:169-184 runs the callbacks before `CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_free`; `engine_table_cleanup` takes the write lock itself).
No re-entrant engine API is active on this thread; B20 records the external contract that engine init/finish/destroy hooks must not re-enter (the crate refuses recursive write acquisition).
what_the_implementation_may_assume: The slot is this module's own process-global `&'static EngineTableSlot`; no caller can substitute another table.
The lhash in the slot and its EnginePile nodes are owned by the slot and released exactly once by `engine_table_cleanup` under the write lock.
A repeated invocation observes the swapped-out NULL slot and performs no release (idempotent by construction).

dispositions.ownership_lifetime: Slot: process-global static owned by the module. Table lhash and EnginePile nodes: owned by the slot, released by `engine_table_cleanup` under the engine write lock (`OPENSSL_LH_doall` + `OPENSSL_LH_free`). Cleanup item: owned by CLEANUP_STACK until `engine_cleanup_cb_free` releases it. The callback borrows no caller data and returns no value.
dispositions.failure_semantics: No return value. If `CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock` fails (including an uninitialised/NULL lock), `engine_table_cleanup` returns before `swap`, leaving the slot populated and the table unreleased (leak/no-op, not UB). If the lock is acquired, the slot is swapped to NULL before any release, so a second call is a no-op. No path performed by this callback can double-free or use-after-free.
dispositions.residual_obligation: Shared callee dependency only: `engine_table_cleanup` (B20-TBL-3) is CONTRACTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED, and its `# Safety` does not state the lock-initialised precondition that the failing control exposes. The wrapper itself has no caller-supplied pointer obligation.

residuals.description: The shared callee `engine_table_cleanup` (B20-TBL-3, CONTRACTED) required an initialised engine lock but its `# Safety` stated only "the engine lock must not already be held". REPAIR: the `# Safety` at src/engine/eng_table.rs:520-532 now states the initialised-lock precondition, the lock-init path, and the exact failure (NULL lock -> returns without swapping/releasing; a no-op/leak, not UB). The boundary now checks `global_engine_lock().is_null()` explicitly (src/engine/eng_table.rs:533-545) instead of relying on `CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(NULL)`, with no behaviour change and no release-mode panic. The nine callbacks (src/engine/tb_*.rs), `engine_cleanup_cb_free` (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:680-686) and `engine_list_cleanup` (src/engine/eng_list.rs:86-97) now state the same precondition, as do the sibling table routines `engine_table_register` (src/engine/eng_table.rs:262-276), `engine_table_unregister` (:459-469) and `ossl_engine_table_select` (:560-573). Production establishes the precondition transitively: every public path that yields an `ENGINE` runs the lock init, and registration is the only way to enqueue the callback. NOT DISCHARGED: independent BOUNDARY review is pending.

C3 failed in isolation at adceec204 and on integrate/safe-c33 because the test omitted `run_engine_lock_init`. REPAIR: the test now calls it (src/engine/eng_table.rs:944-948); C3 passes both isolated and in the module filter, and C8 pins the contrasting uninitialised-lock arm in a fresh process. The idempotence/double-call property is established at the repaired working tree, subject to independent review.

B20-TBL-3 is CONTRACTED with residuals B20-R2 (table entries borrow ENGINE*, no reference) and B20-R3 (authority parity). The wrapper discharge would rest on a CONTRACTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED, dependency.
